sections.overview: Cirrhoscyllium expolitum is a small Northwest Pacific carpet shark in the family Parascylliidae, known from the South China Sea.
sections.identification: The species is known from very few specimens, including a 34 cm female type; throat barbels distinguish the genus from many other carpet sharks.
sections.habitat: Published records place it on the continental shelf of the South China Sea, roughly 180–190 m deep, between southern China and the Philippines.
sections.diet: Its diet is poorly documented; the available sources do not establish a species-specific prey list.
sections.behavior: It is a bottom-dwelling shark, but observations are too limited to describe its daily activity or movement in detail.
sections.reproduction: Available species summaries report egg-laying, although direct reproductive observations are scarce.
sections.ecology: It is one of three recognized Cirrhoscyllium species; compare its South China Sea records with the more localized Taiwanese C. formosanum and Japanese C. japonicum.
sections.conservation: The IUCN assessment lists it as Data Deficient, reflecting the limited distribution, biological and population information available.
